doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: Typecasting Latino composers in Hollywood
summary: He says directors typecast Latino composers as salsa-only, calls it a kind of discrimination, and describes few film opportunities in 14 years in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I’m going to tell you, in general this is going to sound a little rough, but it’s what I really feel. If some people have some kind of stereotyped mentality in terms of jazz music and this and that, also in terms of to pick a composer for a movie, a lot of directors and producers have a stereotype mentality. If you’re a Latino guy like me, I say yes, it’s a little bit of salsa in the thing. “Call Arturo, he could do it.” But if it’s a dramatic thing or something extremely romantic and with a lot of finesse and fine chords and things, they don’t thought about a Latino guy. You know what I call that? A kind of discrimination. A sort of discrimination. It’s what it is. And probably Clint didn’t thought about me to write the whole score, but when I demonstrated to him that I was able to go with the flow and you saw what I mean, and I conveyed my ideas in terms of to please the images and the drama, he changed his mind in two hours. And he said, “Oh my I think, you know what? I was wrong. This guy could do the whole thing.”
Thank you for sharing that. These producers, film producers should listen to your “Second Trumpet Concerto,” that’s what I think.

For me that has been very difficult to have opportunity here in L.A. I live in L.A. for fourteen years. The main reason we moved from Florida to L.A., it was exactly for that, looking for opportunity to write scores. Because it’s probably my biggest passion within the music, writing scores for movies. I love that. I love that more than I can say. And I didn’t have enough opportunity in fourteen years. I did a few movies, a few, very few.

But that’s the thing you know, some people, you know they say oh yeah you need some finesse or something, da-da-da. Okay. Look for some guy from France or Germany or Italy. You understand what I mean? But a Cuban guy? Excuse me, thank you. I still make my living and I shouldn’t complain. I don’t want you getting a wrong concept of how my soul feels you know. And I’m extremely grateful, I’m just telling you what I really feel about all the things, but those things I try my best don’t affect me in general, and don’t discourage me to keep practicing, learning, improving my thing.
